content_voiceover: This is the classic normal platelet aggregation tracing tested on boards. It's a light transmission aggregometry trace after adding low-dose ADP, one micromolar, to platelet-rich plasma. As platelets aggregate, more light passes through, so this inverted optical density axis moves downward. Point one is baseline before the agonist. Point two is shape change, a tiny transient blip as discoid platelets become spiny spheres, before true aggregation starts. Point three marks onset of the primary wave, driven directly by the exogenous ADP. The bracket at four spans that primary aggregation phase. Point five is peak aggregation, where the secondary wave from platelets releasing their own ADP and thromboxane A2 pushes amplitude to maximum. Point six is disaggregation, the gradual decline as aggregates fall apart. Knowing this six-point anatomy, baseline, shape change, primary wave, secondary wave peak, and disaggregation, is the key to reading any aggregometry tracing.
keypoints: 3→4: primary wave = response to exogenous ADP
keypoint_voiceover: Six landmarks: baseline, then shape change, a quick blip before any real aggregation. The primary wave, driven by the ADP you added. Peak aggregation, that's the secondary wave from platelets releasing their own granule contents. And finally disaggregation as the clump falls apart.
